title: The Trial That Changed International Law Forever

sections.name: Hook
lines: n_hook
For the first time ever, the leaders of a defeated regime were put on trial, in front of the whole world.
n_title
This was the Nuremberg trial. And it changed international law forever.

sections.name: One court, four nations
lines: n_flags
In November 1945, the United States, Britain, France, and the Soviet Union set up an international military tribunal.
n_hall
It sat in Nuremberg, Germany, in a courthouse that had survived the bombing.
n_dock
In the dock sat twenty-one of the regime's most senior leaders. One more was tried in his absence.

sections.name: The evidence
lines: n_phones
Every word was translated live, into four languages, through headphones.
n_docs
Prosecutors used the regime's own records against it, and showed film from the concentration camps.

sections.name: No excuse
lines: n_orders
Many of the accused said they had only been following orders.
n_rule
The court said that was no excuse. A person is responsible for their crimes, even under orders.

sections.name: The legacy
lines: n_verdict
In October 1946, twelve were sentenced to death, seven went to prison, and three were acquitted.
n_icc
Its principles shaped the laws on genocide and crimes against humanity. And in 2002, a permanent International Criminal Court opened in The Hague.
d_outro
Follow for more moments from history you won't forget.
